name: Jun Nishida
title: Assistant Professor
fitReason: A narrower assistive/physical human-AI option for CS work on interactive personalization and user-aware feedback. The lab builds on-body devices; interest and skill in experimental HCI and hardware integration matter alongside coding.

physicalEvidence.summary: The official Haptimize project page reports a 2026 system that learns modality-selection values from objective performance and subjective ratings, choosing among electrical muscle stimulation, vibrotactile feedback and an exoskeleton. It reports an 18-person piano-learning study. A separate 2026 FIXical I/O project documents an actual magnetic hand exoskeleton with real-time motion sensing and active physical error interventions; its human motor-learning result must not itself be called machine learning. Current lab and first-author pages establish Kyungyeon Lee as Nishida’s advisee. Full Haptimize manuscript and exact device/control implementation were not available in this pass, so physical points are below a fully inspected deployed-method paper.

shortVisit.summary: The live EmD Join page has a distinct international Research Assistants & Visiting Scholars paragraph and offers to discuss support for international student scholarship applications. This is a broad inquiry route, not a confirmed external-master’s internship. Its linked UMIACS page now resolves to professional-track faculty appointment policies, which does not settle visiting-student eligibility.

scoreReasons.fit: 34/40: learned physical feedback personalization and human-centered AI, but specialized wearable/motor-learning scope.
scoreReasons.physical: 23/25: own-group current physical learning system and separate concrete exoskeleton implementation on primary lab pages; full learned-system manuscript and device specifics remain unverified.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: 5/20: explicit international visiting-scholar inquiry, with student category, duration and summer capacity unresolved.
scoreReasons.freshness: 15/15: distinct substantive 2026 Haptimize and CHI physical-interaction projects establish current activity.
